title: Students clash at Calicut University in Thenhippalam

tea.why: Clashes occurred between student groups during the counting of votes for the campus students' union elections.
tea.want: The protest involves competing student groups and allegations regarding election conduct.
tea.changed: Oct 28: The university suspended classes for two days and postponed election results following the violence.

summary: On October 28, 2026, clashes broke out between the Students' Federation of India (SFI) and the United Democratic Students' Front (UDSF) at the University of Calicut campus in Thenhippalam. The violence occurred during the counting of votes for the campus students' union polls, involving stone-pelting and damage to property, including motorcycles and an election committee office. Police intervened with a lathicharge to disperse the groups. Following the incident, the university registrar suspended classes for undergraduate and postgraduate students for October 29 and 30, directing students to vacate hostels. The university also postponed the announcement of election results and rescheduled internal examinations. SFI leaders later alleged that their members were attacked at a hospital while visiting those injured in the campus clash.
response: Police intervened with a lathicharge to disperse the students and are maintaining a vigil on the campus. The university administration suspended classes for two days and postponed the election results.

injuries.text: According to sources, around 30 students were injured.

updates.text: Clashes between SFI and UDSF activists occurred during vote counting, leading to police intervention and class suspension.
